ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #8
====

GRADE: Grade 2
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

2. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. No full stops
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. Many unrelated topics with no link

4. When practising Pre-reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Pre-reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-reading.

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goes
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. going

6. When practising Letter sound knowledge, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Letter sound knowledge.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Letter sound knowledge.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Letter sound knowledge.

7. When practising Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Comprehension.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Comprehension.

8. When practising Connected text reading and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Connected text reading and fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text reading and fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Connected text reading and fluency.

9. When practising Language structures School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Language structures School.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Language structures School.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Language structures School.

10. When practising Pre- Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Pre- Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre- Writing.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Pre- Writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Pre- Writing.

11. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. happiness
   B. run
   C. blue
   D. quickly

12. When practising Word reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Word reading.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Word reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Word reading.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Punctuation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Attentive listening and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

3. B — One main idea with supporting sentences

4. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-reading.

5. C — went

6. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Letter sound knowledge.

7. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Comprehension.

8. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text reading and fluency.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language structures School.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre- Writing.

11. B — run

12. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word reading.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Attentive listening; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Pronunciation and Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
